title: Request For Information Re: Residential Reentry Services and Home Confinement Services within city limits of Pawtucket, Rhode Island.
description: Request for Proposal (RFP) - 15BRRC26R00000009 Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services and Home Confinement (HC) services for male and female offenders located within city limits of Pawtucket, Rhode Island. Home Confinement radius is within 100 miles of the RRC facility. The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which are located within city limits of Pawtucket, Rhode Island. Home Confinement radius is within 100 miles of the RRC facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four one-year options periods. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 8 beds (8 males and 0 females) and an estimated maximum 20 beds facility in which 18 beds will be designated for males and 2 beds designated for females. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 3 placements and an estimated maximum 8 placements to include both male and female. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000009 will be available on or about August 3, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. Future information about this acquisition will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The estimated closing date of this solicitation (RFP) will be after 60 days around October 2, 2026. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. No telephone request or written requests for the solicitation will be accepted.

description: ***UPDATE 9/2/26: Uploaded Amendment 0001. This Amendment updates Section 00 22 00 to include the Small Business Participation Proposal Worksheet.*** The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Omaha District, hereby announces the solicitation for Gavins Point Intake Crane Rail Replacement. The solicitation will close on 02 October 2026. The solicitation is(Unrestricted and Open to Both Large and Small Business Participation. A Site Visit is scheduled and additional information regarding the site visit is provided in the solicitation via FAR Clause 52.236-27. The site visit is scheduled for 03 September 2026. This project will involve removal and replacement of the Gavins Point Powerhouse Intake crane runway rail located near Yankton, South Dakota. The 80-ton Gavins Point Intake Gantry Crane rail shall be installed and aligned to Crane Manufacturers Association of America, CMAA 70 standards. The total length of the rails is 328 ft x 2 centerline of rail to the powerhouse wall. The work will include an initial survey of the rail alignment, existing grout pocket condition, demolition and removal of existing intake crane rail and components, rail clips, asphalt, base plates, and non-shrink grout. Demolition and removal of the existing concrete anchors will be based on the concrete imaging reports, and the grout pocket condition assessment between each anchor pair along the deck. For bidding purposes, it is assumed 80 percent of the existing anchors will be replaced and all concrete anchors at joint bars will be replaced. The contractor will provide anchors suitable for use in cracked concrete and under seismic loading. Once the rail and hardware are replaced and aligned to the required standards the grout pockets will be filled with two-component aliphatic polyurethane elastomer grout along the full length of the intake crane runway as shown on the drawings. The sequencing of demolition and installation of the crane rails must minimize project time without an operational intake crane and typically progress from one side of the dam to the other with the transfer of the crane from old to new rail during completion of the final rail segment. The Contractor will be required to commence work upon receipt of contract award and complete the work 365 calendar days after receipt of Notice to Proceed, this is subject to change after solicitation issuance. The estimated construction cost of this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The Primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this solicitation is 238120, Structural Steel and Precast Concrete Contractors, with a size standard for Small Business of $19M. All questions shall be submitted on ProjNet (ProjNet access, and additional guidance are contained within the solicitation). The Contracting Office is USACE Omaha District, 1616 Capital Ave, Omaha, NE 68102. The Place of Performance is Gavins Point Project, Crofton, NE 68730.

title: Weapons Generation Facility, Dyess AFB OT Feasibility & Business Feedback
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought Notice/RFI � Weapons Generation Facility, Dyess AFB DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought (SS) is for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP) or an Invitation for Bids (IFB). This notice is issued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a (Other Transaction Authority for Construction and Repair) and is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). No solicitation is available at this time. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The planned procurement will construct a secure Weapons Generation Facility (WGF) complex at Dyess Air Force Base, Texas, supporting an Air Force Global Strike Command (AFGBSC) mission. The project entails constructing a complex of multiple hardened facilities within a protective zone, totaling approximately 77,000 SF. Key elements include the following: Primary Facilities: Special Weapons Maintenance Shop, Entry Control Facility, Alert Fire Team Facility, Fire Pump Building, Diesel Generator Building, Remote Tracking and Engagement System (RTES) Towers. Specialized Infrastructure: Six 5-ton overhead bridge cranes (five nuclear-certifiable), emergency power generation, physical security fencing, and foundation systems engineered to accommodate local expansive soils. Design & Delivery Parameters: The design is currently at 65% completion (Code 6). The Air Force intends to retain the current Designer of Record (DoR) through project completion, requiring direct collaboration with the retained DoR. Budget & Schedule: The Target Construction Cost (TCC) is $246,820,000, with incremental funding beginning in FY28. Construction Completion Date (CCD) is targeted for December 2031, with Beneficial Occupancy (BOD) targeted for June 2032. INSTRUCTIONS TO INDUSTRY Review Attached Project Information Packet (PIP): Interested firms are directed to review the attached document. This packet provides comprehensive project requirements, constraints, and the complete questionnaire reference. Submit Responses via Microsoft Forms: To streamline the collection and analysis of industry feedback, responses to the market research questionnaire must be submitted electronically via the following link: Online Feedback Form: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/RNedjtbkkn Response Due Date: All electronic responses must be submitted via the online form no later than October 2, 2026, at 2:00 PM Central Time (CT). description: Pre-Solicitation Notice (Updated) Solicitation Number: 140R3026R0012 Title: Yuma Desalting Plant (YDP) Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Support Services IDIQ This is an updated Pre-Solicitation Notice for Solicitation 140R3026R0012, superseding the notice originally posted in July 2026. The anticipated issuance date, site visit timeframe, and set-aside description have been revised. All dates in this notice are estimates and are subject to change. Specific instructions on submitting your proposal will be contained in the solicitation documents to be issued on or about September 01, 2026, posted to the SAM.gov website. No documents will be available until the solicitation is issued. The U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), Bureau of Reclamation (Reclamation), Lower Colorado Basin, Yuma Area Office, has a requirement for a five (5) year Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract type for Operation and Maintenance (O&M) support services for the Yuma Desalting Plant (YDP) and Water Quality Improvement Center (WQIC). The Contractor shall furnish day-to-day plant operations and maintenance for the Yuma Desalting Plant on a 24-hour basis. The ready reserve status ensures that the plant receives the required planned maintenance needed to maintain the plant in the event the plant converts to a fully operational mode. The acquisition plan does not forecast an immediate need for full operational capacity of the plant during this contract period, but there is the option for a level of effort that will allow a short-term demonstration run for various percentages of capacity, e.g., 33%, 66%, and 100%. The services will take place in Yuma, Yuma County, Arizona. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with this requirement is 561210 � Facilities Support Services. The small business size standard applicable to this project is $47.0 million. The projected IDIQ ceiling amount is $35,000,000.00, representing the maximum cumulative value of all task orders issued under this contract. This requirement will be issued as a 100% 8(a) Alaskan Native Corporation-Owned Firm Set-Aside. The solicitation will be awarded using the methods outlined in the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) deviations to FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, and FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. A site visit is tentatively scheduled for the last week in September 2026; however, please refer to the solicitation for official details when posted. An electronic copy of the solicitation will be issued no sooner than fifteen (15) days from the day after this notice at www.sam.gov; however, dates in this notice are subject to change. Any amendments applicable to the solicitation will be posted at the same site. To take advantage of business opportunities with the Bureau of Reclamation (BOR) and the Department of the Interior (DOI), your entity must be registered in SAM.gov. For more information regarding registering in SAM, please visit https://sam.gov/content/entity-registration. This notice is not a request for proposals. No proposals will be accepted at this time. All instructions, the Statement of Work, and additional attachments will be included in the formal solicitation. title: Gavins Point Crane Rail Replacement
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Omaha District, hereby announces the solicitation for Gavins Point Intake Crane Rail Replacement. The solicitation will close on 02 October 2026. The solicitation is(Unrestricted and Open to Both Large and Small Business Participation. A Site Visit is scheduled and additional information regarding the site visit is provided in the solicitation via FAR Clause 52.236-27. The site visit is scheduled for 03 September 2026. This project will involve removal and replacement of the Gavins Point Powerhouse Intake crane runway rail located near Yankton, South Dakota. The 80-ton Gavins Point Intake Gantry Crane rail shall be installed and aligned to Crane Manufacturers Association of America, CMAA 70 standards. The total length of the rails is 328 ft x 2 centerline of rail to the powerhouse wall. The work will include an initial survey of the rail alignment, existing grout pocket condition, demolition and removal of existing intake crane rail and components, rail clips, asphalt, base plates, and non-shrink grout. Demolition and removal of the existing concrete anchors will be based on the concrete imaging reports, and the grout pocket condition assessment between each anchor pair along the deck. For bidding purposes, it is assumed 80 percent of the existing anchors will be replaced and all concrete anchors at joint bars will be replaced. The contractor will provide anchors suitable for use in cracked concrete and under seismic loading. Once the rail and hardware are replaced and aligned to the required standards the grout pockets will be filled with two-component aliphatic polyurethane elastomer grout along the full length of the intake crane runway as shown on the drawings. The sequencing of demolition and installation of the crane rails must minimize project time without an operational intake crane and typically progress from one side of the dam to the other with the transfer of the crane from old to new rail during completion of the final rail segment. The Contractor will be required to commence work upon receipt of contract award and complete the work 365 calendar days after receipt of Notice to Proceed, this is subject to change after solicitation issuance. The estimated construction cost of this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The Primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this solicitation is 238120, Structural Steel and Precast Concrete Contractors, with a size standard for Small Business of $19M. All questions shall be submitted on ProjNet (ProjNet access, and additional guidance are contained within the solicitation). The Contracting Office is USACE Omaha District, 1616 Capital Ave, Omaha, NE 68102. The Place of Performance is Gavins Point Project, Crofton, NE 68730.

The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. title: OCIE-Southeast 3PL
description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support, Clothing and Textiles (C&T) Directorate, anticipates the award of a Firm-Fixed Price Service contract with an Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) allowed for standard freight shipments, for Third Party Logistics (3PL) support. This initiative represents the Organization Clothing and Individual Equipment (OCIE) Southeast 3PL Program, a DLA Troop Support initiative to furnish warehousing, storage, inventory management and distribution functions for DLA Troop Support, and its� military customers. The purpose of this initiative is to satisfy customer requisitions for military service C&T items including boots, coats, parkas, helmets, foot lockers, and body armor. The Contractor will not be responsible for requisitioning clothing from the manufacturing community. Rather, DLA Troop Support will procure the replenishment quantities and advise manufacturers to ship directly to the Contractor. The apparel to be stored will be Government owned materiel. The apparel and equipment items to be stored will be Government owned materiel. The current program procedures are as follows: The 3PL Contractor receives apparel and equipment item shipments daily from item manufacturers, other 3PLs and U.S Government supply depots; warehouses the items; and ships directly to C&T customers located both in the Continental U.S. (CONUS) and Outside the Continental U.S. (OCONUS). The acquisition will be conducted in accordance with FAR 15 and FAR part 12 under full and open competition on an unrestricted basis. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. title: Market Research for Survivability, Assured Mobility, and Maneuver Support
description: Market Research for research and development (R&D) efforts on various aspects related to Survivability, Assured Mobility, and Maneuver Support material solutions. The term Survivability encompasses those actions, materiel, and design solutions that give commanders occupant centric survivability through the maturation and integration of technology. Survivability technologies include, but are not limited to, armor, fire protection, hit avoidance, laser protection, countermine, active and passive protection systems, and occupant interior protection. The term "Assured Mobility" encompasses those actions, materiel, and design solutions that give commanders the ability to deploy, move, and maneuver assets where and when they desire, without interruption or delay, to achieve the mission. The imperatives and principles of Assured Mobility are what will enable future forces to have superior situational understanding and, therefore, unsurpassed freedom of movement in global terrain and climate profiles, including, but not limited to, tropical, arid, temperate, continental, and polar. The term "Maneuver Support" encompasses those actions, materiel, and design solutions that give commanders the ability to maintain an unprecedented level of freedom of movement at the tactical, operational, and strategic levels in all environments. Materiel items most relevant to Maneuver Support efforts include survivability, countermine, track and suspension, power management, robotics, bridging systems and combat engineer equipment for the freedom to maneuver through constructed obstacles, unstructured terrain, and for the interrogation of improvised explosive devices (IEDs) and route clearance (mobility and counter-mobility operations).

title: Germany – Engineering design services – Gemeinde Stralendorf - Neubau der Kindertagesstätte "Regenbogen"
description: Die Gemeinde Stralendorf (Eigentümer/Bauherr) plant den Neubau der Kindertagesstätte Regenbogen als Ersatz für die bestehende Einrichtung als eigenständiges Gebäude auf dem direkt angrenzenden Grundstück für 40 Kinder (28 Kindergarten- und 12 Krippenkinder). Durch den geplanten Neubau sollen sich die Betreuungs- und Rahmenbedingungen für die Kinder und Erzieherinnen verbessern. Im neuen Gebäude ist geplant, 1 Krippenbereich für 12 Kinder sowie 2 Kitabereiche für je 14 Kinder anzubieten, so dass insgesamt 40 Kinder die Einrichtung in Stralendorf besuchen können. Die Möglichkeit einer Erweiterung um 8 Kinder (1 Mischgruppe) soll hierbei Berücksichtigung finden. Die geplante Nettogrundfläche von 328 qm entspricht der maximal zulässigen Fläche für die Entgeldberechnung. Als Gebäudestandort wird das vorhandene Grundstück (Flurstück 135/21, Flur 2) mit einer Größe von ca. 1.600 qm genutzt, ohne die bestehenden Freiflächen und -anlagen der jetzigen Kindertagesstätte zu beeinträchtigen. Diese bleiben erhalten und sollen weiterhin als Außenspielflächen genutzt werden. Das Ortsbild der Gemeinde ist in diesem Bereich durch eingeschossige Gebäude mit Sattel- und Krüppelwalmdächern sowie Nebengebäude und Anbauten mit unterschiedlichen Dachformen geprägt. Der geplante eingeschossige Baukörper der neuen Kindertagesstätte mit den flach geneigten Satteldächern soll sich harmonisch in das Dorfbild einfügen. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind Ingenieurleistungen gemäß HOAI 2021 Teil 4 Fachplanung, Abschnitt 1 Tragwerksplanung, Leistungsphasen 1 - 4, Leistungsphase 5-6 optional (Stufenvertrag). Die Beauftragung der Stufe 1 (LPH 1-4) erfolgt sofort, die Beauftragung der Stufe 2 (LPH 5-6) erfolgt nach Bewilligung von Fördermitteln. Ein Anspruch des Auftragnehmers auf die Beauftragung der Stufe 2 besteht nicht.

description: Beabsichtigt ist die Beauftragung von Generalplanungsleistungen mit folgenden Leistungsbildern: -Leistungsbild Generalplanungsmanagement, -Objektplanungsleitungen für Gebäude und Innenräume nach Teil 3, Abschnitt 1 HOAI, LPH 2,3,5-8 und Besondere Leistungen, -Objektplanungsleistungen für Ingenieurbauwerke nach Teil 3 Abschnitt 3 HOAI, LPH 2,3,5-8, -Objektplanungsleistungen für Verkehrsanlagen nach Teil 3 Abschnitt 4 HOAI, LPH 2,3,5-8, -Fachplanungsleistungen für Tragwerksplanung nach Teil 4, Abschnitt 1 HOAI, für LPH 2-6 und Besondere Leistungen LST 4, -Fachplanungsleistungen für Technische Ausrüstung nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 2 HOAI, für Anlagengruppen 1-5 und 8, für LPH 2,3,5-8 und Besondere Leistungen. Aufgabenbeschreibung: Die Ausschreibung umfasst Generalplanungsleistungen für die Anpassung der Wasserversorgung inklusive Prüfung des Pumpwerks Sylvenstal in der Staufer-Kaserne Pfullendorf. Die Wasserversorgung der Staufer-Kaserne Pfullendorf war in der Vergangenheit wiederholt von mikrobiologischen Beeinträchtigungen betroffen und soll daher angepasst werden. Hierfür ist zunächst ein Planungskonzept zu erarbeiten. In der Zulaufstrecke soll ein Gebäude für die Unterbringung der Aufbereitungstechnik neu errichtet werden. Die Aufbereitungstechnik wird voraussichtlich eine Druckerhöhungsanlage mit nachgeschalteter Enthärtung (Prinzip: Ionentauscher mit Soletank und nachgeschalteter Dosierung) und UV-C Lichtdesinfektion beinhalten. Das bestehende System der Gebäudeautomation ist zu überprüfen und soweit zu ertüchtigen, dass ein Fernzugriff auf die Pumpe im bestehenden Pumpwerk mit entsprechendem Datenaustausch ermöglicht wird. Die Gesamtkosten der Baumaßnahme betragen ca. 1.620.000 € brutto (geschätzte Kosten der Kostengruppen 200-600 nach DIN 276:2018-12). Planungsbeginn: 12/2026, Baubeginn: 04/2028, Fertigstellung: 08/2029. Weitere Informationen zur geplanten Baumaßnahme können Sie der zip-Datei"26-21235_Angebotsunterlagen zunächst nur informativ" entnehmen.

description: Cette procédure, définie par les art. R. 812-1 et suivants du code de l'énergie, a pour objet la sélection des bénéficiaires du dispositif de soutien pour les filières de production d’hydrogène bas-carbone par électrolyse de l'eau ou d'hydrogène renouvelable sur le territoire français. Les modalités d’octroi de l’aide seront précisées dans le cahier des charges établi à l’issue de la phase de sélection des candidats éligibles à participer à la procédure. L’aide portera sur une durée maximale de 15 ans. Il s’agit de la deuxième vague du régime d’aide SA.101951 ayant fait l’objet d’une décision de la Commission européenne. La procédure de mise en concurrence décrite aux articles R. 812-1 et suivants du code de l'énergie comprend une phase de sélection des candidats éligibles, et une phase de désignation des lauréats, parmi les candidats retenus, pour bénéficier du soutien. À l’issue de la phase de sélection des candidats éligibles, un cahier des charges sera adressé aux candidats en vue de la remise des demandes d’aides finales et de la sélection des Lauréats. Sous réserve des articles L. 2224- 32 et L. 2224-33 du code général des collectivités territoriales, toute personne installée sur le territoire d'un État membre de l'union européenne ou, dans le cadre de l'exécution d'accords internationaux, sur le territoire de tout autre État couvert par un tel accord et désirant construire et exploiter une unité de production sur le territoire français peut participer à cette procédure de mise en concurrence. Cet avis répond aux conditions de l'article R. 812-4 du code de l'énergie. Calendrier prévisionnel de la procédure : les documents de la consultation seront disponibles sur le site de l'ADEME à partir du 01/09/2026. La date limite de dépôt des candidatures est le 02/10/2026 (23h59). La date prévisionnelle de désignation des candidats éligibles à déposer une offre est le 02/11/2026. Pour plus de détails, voir document de consultation

title: Germany – Roof-covering work – Grundschule Wagenstadt - Dachdeckung, Dachabdichtung und Klempnerarbeiten
description: Gegenstand der Ausschreibung sind Dachdeckungs-, Dachabdichtungs- und Klempnerarbeiten für die Sanierung und Erweiterung der Grundschule Wagenstadt in Herbolzheim. Die Leistungen umfassen Rückbau- und Demontagearbeiten an bestehenden Dachaufbauten, die Herstellung von Stehfalzdächern und Sandwicheindeckungen, Dachentwässerungsarbeiten, Flachdachabdichtungen einschließlich Dachbegrünung sowie die Lieferung und Montage von Dachsicherungssystemen. Ausführung geplant in KW 29 - KW 40. Die Grundschule Wagenstadt wurde in den 1960er Jahren als dreigeschossiges Schulgebäude ohne Unterkellerung errichtet. Westlich des Hauptgebäudes wurde 1998 ein eingeschossiger Erweiterungsbau ergänzt; zudem erfolgten bereits Umbaumaßnahmen im Bestand. Im Rahmen einer umfassenden Sanierung und Erweiterung wird die Schule über einen Zeitraum von rund eineinhalb Jahren modernisiert. Das Bestandsgebäude erhält ein zusätzliches Dachgeschoss mit Satteldach sowie ein vollflächiges Wärmedämmverbundsystem mit vorgehängter Fassade. Hierfür wird das Gebäude bis auf den Rohbau entkernt und anschließend grundlegend saniert. Ergänzend entstehen ein südlich angeordneter Neubau in Stahlbetonbauweise sowie ein neues Treppenhaus nördlich des Bestandsgebäudes, das als zweiter baulicher Rettungsweg dient und den Zugang zum neuen Dachgeschoss ermöglicht. Darüber hinaus wird ein Aufzug eingebaut, der alle Geschosse vom Erdgeschoss bis zum 2. Obergeschoss erschließt. Beide Anbauten werden ohne Unterkellerung auf Pfahlgründungen errichtet. Im Zuge der Bauausführung ist die Grundbruchsicherheit des Bestandsgebäudes insbesondere bei der Herstellung der südlich und östlich gelegenen Baugruben und Verbaumaßnahmen sicherzustellen.

This work covers the 41 countries participating in the European Comparison Programme (ECP): EU Member States, EFTA/EEA countries, enlargement countries and the UK. The policy relevance and use of PPPs lie in their role in converting national accounts aggregates into comparable volume measures and in analysing relative price levels across EU countries. This requires high-quality PPP data. These requirements put very strong emphasis on the collection of comparable price data across countries, the validation of the data, and the methodology applied for calculating the PPPs. All according to detailed and agreed time-schedules for the releases of the PPPs. The work on equipment goods prices requires technical knowledge of machinery, electronic and other equipment that is not available at Eurostat. description: ++++++++++++++++++++ Es wird ausdrücklich darauf hingewiesen, dass entgegen § 41 Abs. 1 SektVO die Vergabeunterlagen nicht vollständig sind und die Leistungsbeschreibung inkl. title: Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) Call for Whitepapers for Mission Development Zone (MDZ) Outgrant
description: 1. DESCRIPTION 1.1. Growth of the U.S. Domestic Space industry has resulted in a greater demand for use of real property at U.S. Space Force (USSF) Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30), Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) by private and commercial entities to conduct spaceport support, payload processing, hardware manufacturing, testing, logistics, and other space-related activities. Ensuring that United States operators can efficiently process space systems, conduct missions in space, launch, and reenter United States airspace is critical to economic growth, national security, and accomplishing Federal space objectives. 1.2. SLD 30 requests white paper responses from United States Commercial Providers as defined by 51 U.S.C. � 50101(7) engaged in space transportation, spaceport support, spacecraft manufacturing, payload processing, assembly, test, space logistics, or other space-related operations on the buildout of the Mission Development Zone (MDZ). Respondents will offer insights, perspectives, and approaches to obtain real property-use agreements to finance, design, construct, operate, and maintain spaceport infrastructure. Industry insights from whitepaper submissions may be utilized to drive future RFI / RFP announcements issued by SLD 30. Specifically, the MDZ infrastructure is intended to provide critical support services to the Department of War (DoW), commercial spaceflight, and other spaceport users at an undeveloped area located in the southern region of VSFB�s North Base area. Development and utilization of the MDZ will be in support of maximizing spaceport capability and assured access to space to achieve national security objectives. 1.3. Description of Premises is at Exhibit B. Please note that the MDZ is not a space launch complex (launch pad), but rather a flexible development zone dedicated to supporting the broader spaceport ecosystem. This includes, but is not limited to, payload processing, hazardous processing, spaceport logistics, commodity storage, launch and mission control, research and development, spacecraft integration, and administrative/engineering spaces. 1.4. The USSF is gathering market intelligence to determine the feasibility of a future real property outgrant under 10 U.S.C. � 2667 to a commercial space services provider, spaceport support provider, launch service provider (LSP), space infrastructure provider, or other space-related entity to construct spaceport-related support infrastructure. MDZ support infrastructure may include, but is not limited to, the following activities: processing, manufacturing, logistics, and administrative support activities. Data gathered from white paper responses will directly inform the Government in determining optimal MDZ utilization and potential infrastructure requirements to meet Government and industry launch requirements. 1.5. To support its ongoing spaceport capacity expansion, Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30) continuously evaluates opportunities and fields requests for new missions. Accordingly, SLD 30 provides discretionary site access and information to prospective partners at any time. Spaceport users and providers responding to this call for whitepapers wishing to view the site may request a property viewing. Please note that scheduling a site visit does not constitute grounds for extending the submittal deadline. 2. CONDITIONS 2.1. This call for whitepapers is not governed by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and is not a Request for Information (RFI), a Request for Proposal (RFP), a Request for Quote (RFQ), nor a solicitation announcement. Content of whitepapers will provide industry insight to assist the Government in scoping, planning, and defining requirements for the proposed MDZ. Content of the whitepapers may assist the Government in generating future contract requirements. Submitters agree and allow the USSF to use the information in the submissions for this purpose. 2.2. This call for whitepapers is issued solely for informational and planning purposes, and the Government is under no obligation to allocate property. The information contained herein is current as of the publication date but subject to change; it is not binding and may be amended in the future. While SLD 30 intends to review submissions, it is under no obligation to do so and reserves the right to cancel or amend the call for whitepapers at its sole discretion. 2.3. No funds are available to fund the whitepaper requested and the Government will not pay or reimburse any costs associated with responding to this request. 2.4. Any future facility where energetic propellants, hazardous materials, and/or ordnance will be used, processed, or stored will require the development of an explosives site plan. To assist the Government in layout and zoning analysis, respondents should outline any anticipated explosive safety arcs, quantity-distance (QD) requirements, or specialized hazard mitigation constraints. 3. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS To assist the U.S. Space Force in scoping and planning for the Mission Development Zone (MDZ), respondents are requested to provide a whitepaper that addresses the following areas. The goal is to gather information on industry needs, operational concepts, and technical requirements to shape the future development of the MDZ. 3.1. Spaceport, Support, and Related Infrastructure Capability. To meet future U.S. Government and commercial space requirements, the USSF seeks to establish robust spaceport support and related infrastructure at VSFB. The MDZ, positioned in the southern area of North VSFB, has been assessed as a potentially viable location for development of infrastructure required for the preparation, operation, and support of launch programs, spacecraft assembly, payload processing, space logistics, and other supporting commercial or industrial activities that enable the spaceport ecosystem. The Government is seeking insights from industry regarding the MDZ layout and planned utilization including types of facilities that would be most beneficial to launch providers in this location. Respondents should provide an assessment with respect to the compatibility of the property with proposed concept of operations. To assist the Government in understanding this capability, respondents should provide a list of all desired facility developments intended to be constructed at the MDZ. 3.2. Payload Processing and Hardware Requirements. A primary objective of the MDZ development is to address current installation capacity constraints regarding payload processing. If a respondent�s concept of operations involves payload or hardware processing, the Government requests specific information regarding requirements to process modern 5-meter-class payloads and next-generation fairings. Respondents should describe necessary facility specifications to include cleanroom class ratings (e.g., ISO 7, ISO 8), overhead crane hook heights, clear span ceiling heights, and projected annual processing throughput. (Note: If a respondent�s proposed operations do not involve payload processing, this section may be omitted). 3.3. Benefit to the Spaceport Ecosystem. Respondents should describe how their proposed operations, facilities, or infrastructure developments will benefit the broader VSFB spaceport ecosystem, the commercial space industry, and U.S. Space Force national security objectives. 3.4. Parcel Selection, Layout Preferences, & Utility Requirements. The MDZ contains roughly 2,100 acres divided into general parcel sizes. The MDZ is located within 5 miles of Vandenberg Airfield with some parcels in the aircraft arrival corridor which will limit building height. To inform the base's Area Development Plan (ADP), respondents are requested to outline their estimated land and utility requirements: Acreage and Parcel Selection: Respondents may address any number of parcels depending on the overall size needed for the discussion of the whitepaper; there is no upper limit to the request. title: Z2NZ--631-19-002 Upgrade Steam Distribution System Phase II Industry Day Recap
description: 631-19-002 Upgrade Steam Distribution System Phase 2 Industry Day Recap Understand Challenges for construction regarding this project from a contractor s perspective. Is there any ability to alter phasing? VA Response: In-short, yes. As a result of your inquiries the project team is proposing phasing to turn over both basement and first floor wings coordinate well in advance to close, relocate, or adjust clinical operations for a fixed period. This includes a lengthy shut down of the canteen in summer months. This will allow more day shift work, more sustained/efficient construction avoiding nightly restoration. With careful planning and temporary heat provision plans by contractor this could also permit work during heating season. The solicitation will contain an updated phasing supplement by wings with permissible down time that shall supersede any specification or drawing phasing plans. We anticipate evaluating proposals with at least 1 factor demonstrating a contractor s utilization of these updates to indicate their time and cost savings relative to off-hours work. This supplement will also include operation constraints such as audiology and pharmacy where noisy work and infection control issues will push to off hours work. When is this project going to be solicited? VA Response: The intention is for this to be solicited late quarter three or quarter four. This presents an excellent opportunity for the awardee to utilize the winter of 26/27 to procure materials, complete admin and detailed coordination drawings for building 1, while utilizing immediately available work in buildings 15 and 16 to establish team dynamics, rhythm, and process to build steam. Are there any specific needs of the facility? Can a contractor utilize temporary heaters? Can a contractor bring in an engineering team to help assist? VA Response: VA would be willing to review these proposed methods. Again, the expectation is for a best value solicitation. The VA is highly motivated to complete this critical infrastructure. We will gladly review RFIs and evaluate tradeoffs. Topics so far we would happy to entertain: Value engineering proposal to change any load to hydronic. Rough sizing calcs demonstrating heating loads are satisfied Advantages: Copper/pluming work vs schedule 80 pipe welding. Significant pipe size reduction in mains, elimination of traps and maintenance costs long term, elimination of gravity dependent pathways. Elimination of smaller condensate pumps such as PTOT, customer care suite, canteen, mech room (still one in sub-basement), elimination of canteen CP by Walk-in. Savings proposals based on phasing supplement and temp heating to allow more winter work. Proposal to include products such as dryers and low maintenance sustainment. Any proposals increasing serviceable and low maintenance sustainment or energy rebate alternative ideas could be considered under best value Rathert than working above drop ceilings propose potential ceiling replacements if phasing supplement turns over. E.G: Canteen just demo drop ceiling to save demo and construction efforts, especially with ACM. Establish new IAW specifications. Propose net savings/cost trade off Canteen store drop ceiling replace Section of hallway leading to canteen, proposed elimination with cosmetic clean up Has the VA confirmed the pipe sizing and gravity of the system? VA Response: The VA has performed a qualitative review and directed drawing updates based on sizing. It is believed the current new work plan is largely oversized without being excessive, but to our knowledge no quantitative analysis exists. Is there any consideration to move away from the non-destructive testing? There are potential pitfalls in utilizing this method. VA Response: VA will look at this and review the methods. The current thought process is to establish minimal surveillance or critical areas where NDT including radiation exclusion radius/sphere will be performed off hours. This will likely be a hybrid between the standard specification and more than B31.1 would typically require. It could also include requirement to document process for items like socket weld (e.g. construction photo showing insertion scribe and back off . Has the VA looked at the potential use of swing spaces? Other VA s have utilized this approach to allow large areas to be vacated in an effort to provide uninterrupted work. VA Response: The utilization of swing spaces is being explored. VA will provide an updated phasing supplement with the solicitation. Is there the ability block off more rooms at a time to avoid the need to restore rooms each day? VA Response: This could be considered. The updated phasing supplement will be provided with the solicitation. Can the Canteen be down for an extended period of time? VA Response: VA is looking into potentially shutting this down for a period of time to allow efficient work. The updated phasing supplement will be provided with the solicitation. How would the VA handle unforeseen asbestos? Is there the ability to utilize a unit price? VA Response: This could be a potential line item for the solicitation. Has the VA looked at reducing the requirement for a degreed engineer for the MEP Coordinator, or all other disciplines? VA Response: VA will take a look at the requirements, but having a qualified MEP Coordinator on this specific job is the intention. Is there the ability for an administrative NTP to be issued? This would allow for more thorough site investigations and planning. It appears that in order to do a proper investigation and coordination drawings the period would need to be longer than the one-hundred and twenty (120) days in the specifications. VA Response: VA will take this under consideration. The intention is that the project will be solicited soon with the target of awarding the project at the beginning of Quarter 1. Historically this period is not well utilized by prime contractors. However, an evaluation factor with major milestones schedule and Proposed Period of Performance would be likely for this project resulting in the intent of this question and maximum flexibility for the prime contractor. The VA would greatly value any commitment that documents the bulk of the administrative data and planning before mobilizing; we believe this is best value for the government and the prime contractor. Understand the major cost drivers. Could a mega-press be used on lower PSI distributions? This has the potential to lower the costs as the need for welders would be minimized VA Response: VA is willing to entertain alternative methods so long as they meet the requirements of the contract and specifications. This would need to be an RFI, there are issues when schedule 80 is called for. If allowed it will likely have size limitations for condensate and smaller for LP steam. Could condensers be stainless steel? They save on weight and performance is similar to what is in the specifications. VA Response: VA would be willing to entertain alternative methods so long as they meet the requirements of the contract and specifications. Deviations or value engineering proposals deviating to above and beyond such as stainless steel can be considered pre award depending on solicitation details What if any value engineering ideas should be considered. Would the VA consider adding moisture separators into the project? Although they are not included adding them in would allow for extended warranties on equipment, there are additional costs associated with adding them in. VA Response: VA would be willing to review any value engineered ideas during the solicitation stage so long as they meet the requirements of the contract and specifications and provide added value to the government for reduced costs, reduced construction time or impact, reduced maintenance, better reliability, or control. description: The Government intends to acquire Rogue Fitness strength and conditioning equipment from Rogue Fitness. The equipment is required to expand and complement the existing tactical physical conditioning facility, which is built around Rogue Fitness racks, rigs, attachments, and related structural components. Rogue Fitness equipment is required because the requested items must safely integrate with the existing Rogue Fitness infrastructure, including specific tubing dimensions, rack and rig dimensions, hole spacing, attachment points, pin and bolt sizes, and manufacturer-rated load-bearing components. Use of non-Rogue or third-party components may result in improper fit, alignment, locking, or load-bearing performance, creating unacceptable safety, structural, warranty, and operational risks. The total estimated value of the requirement is $19,037.06, including shipping. The Government has determined that Rogue Fitness equipment is necessary to meet its minimum needs for compatibility, safety, structural reliability, warranty protection, and continued mission readiness. Interested parties that believe they can satisfy the requirement may submit capability information demonstrating their ability to provide the required Rogue Fitness brand-name items, or fully compatible items that meet the Government�s minimum compatibility, safety, warranty, and operational requirements. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

Y1DA--573-21-106 EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades and Data Center Construction - Gainesville VAMC
description: INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting bids and subsequently awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract for the design-bid-build EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades and Data Center Construction project at the Gainesville VA Medical Center located at 1601 Southwest Archer Road, Gainesville, FL 32608. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The scope of this project is to replace all data infrastructure across the Gainesville VAMC and to build a new data center to support that upgraded system. The data center building will be one story, and the footprint will be approximately 3,931 SF at the location of temporary trailer 11, which will be demolished as part of this project. The primary space within the building is the 1,177 SF Data Center Room. Supporting spaces include Unpacking/Packing/Staging, Entrance Room, and Storage. Mechanical, Electrical, and HVAC spaces. Additionally, a new generator will be housed in a separate Generator Room. Also, this project will be removing all existing equipment and cabling affiliated with the telecom rooms in all campus buildings. There are 59 telecom rooms that may require architectural work. Some rooms are existing TRs being reused, but most are new rooms being redesigned for the telecom equipment. In rare cases telecom enclosures are recommended and/or exceptions will be required. The entire campus will be occupied while work occurs. Contractor will have to coordinate room closures and shutdowns with the COR. Most rooms on campus will be affected. Some off-hour work is anticipated for more critical spaces. ADMINISTRATIVE The solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bids (IFB) conducted in accordance with FAR part 14 and will be evaluated in accordance with the procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in mid to late July 2026, with an estimated late September 2026 award. title: This effort encompasses all technical, logistical, software and hardware efforts required to produce CCS Meadowlands systems.
description: Purpose: This is a Sources Sought. The Space Systems Command (SSC) located at Los Angeles Air Force Base, California, is seeking information in the form of Statements of Capabilities (SOC) from interested parties in support of the SSC, Space Domain Awareness and Combat Power Directorate requirement for the Counter Communications System (CCS) Meadowlands as described below. The Government is conducting market research to inform its Acquisition Strategy. The purpose of this notice is to identify potential sources that can meet CFC/MD3�s requirement. The Government reserves the right to set this acquisition, or portions thereof, aside for small business � to include socially and economically disadvantaged businesses, 8(a) firms, or woman-owned businesses. The Government is seeking contractors interested in and capable of providing all technical and logistical effort required to design, develop, and deliver capabilities to support the CCS Meadowlands system. Background and Description: Scope: This effort encompasses all technical, logistical, software and hardware efforts required to produce CCS Meadowlands systems. Period and Place of Performance: It is envisioned that the period of performance will be approximately 12 months in duration. The Government is working through the details to determine when the contract will start. The place of performance is flexible to allow contractor to provide an optimized solution. Background: CCS System: CCS is a ground-based counter satellite communications (SATCOM) system specifically designed to reversibly deny, disrupt, and degrade adversarial SATCOM. The basic CCS concept is to provide a flexible, modular, scalable, rapidly deployable system with a key set of signal processing/generation (SP) capabilities, selected counter SATCOM missions, and a robust transmit capability. Its architecture will be designed to host core capabilities and/or other more sophisticated �plug and play� type modules to address the ever-increasing number of technologies and assets available to our adversaries. The latest CCS Meadowlands will have upgraded capabilities compared to the existing CCS 10.2 Systems. The future CCS Meadowlands fleet will be composed of at least 32 systems. Meadowlands is a transportable SATCOM system composed of modular Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) / Government Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) Radio Frequency (RF) monitoring and generation equipment. The design incorporates multi-band antennas and equipment in transit cases. The frequency conversion system (FCS) that handles RF signals between the shelter transit cases to the antenna uses a proprietary photonics system. The system can be transported by C-130 or larger aircraft and by ground transport over improved or semi-improved roads. The system will be designed for operations by trained operators in US-controlled facilities world-wide, and in the Developmental Support Facility (DSF). The Meadowlands �Base Design� system meets current A-spec requirements. All systems have same Transit Case and Antenna configuration/capability. The Meadowlands base design system is comprised of the following major capabilities: Three independent, bidirectional antenna polarization paths Native Support for a single Large Multiband Antenna (LMA) Bands Supported: UHF, L, C, Ku, Ka Two separate independently controlled antenna polarization paths Simultaneous dual polarization operation Receive-only operation if desired Supports Base, and unique network specific missions Native Support for a single 1.2m Antenna Antenna Supports L-Band only The system can operate in three antenna Polarization Paths � Each Polarization Path Contains an Uplink & Downlink RF Interface. The system is capable of simultaneously operating/controlling up to three antennas and associated components utilizing three polarization paths. The Meadowlands system utilizes Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Ethernet, TCP & UDP/IP Standard interfaces for network communications (Data, Command, Control & Status) between Transit case assemblies, Antennas and the Software Server The Base System Configuration is composed of: 4 System Transit Cases in Shelter (Mission Control & Timing (MCT) Subsystem, Advanced Signal Processor (ASP) Subsystem, Shelter Photonics Unit (SPU1), SPU2) 1 Antenna Transit Case in Shelter for 1.2m Antenna (1.2m Transit Case) 1 Transit Case for Secure External Network Operations (Remote Ops Transit Case) � Contains Firewall & Encryption 2 Transit Cases outside by LMA antenna (Antenna Photonics Unit (APU)2 & APU2) APU Transit Cases The system can operate in the UHF, L, C, Ku, and KA RF Bands for Transmit and Receive via Frequency Conversion System (FCS) The production of the CCS Meadowlands units has been accomplished as part of a Pre-Planned Product Improvement effort. The program utilizes equipment from the CCS Block 10.2 systems as Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) including the LMA Antenna (Including Servo Controller, Feeds, High Powered Amplifiers (HPAs), Dummy Loads); the 1.2m Antenna (Including Servo Controller, Feeds, HPAs, Dummy Loads), Power Distribution Units (PDUs) (in transit cases) and also external PDUs, Environmental Control Units (ECUs), Tent, and a Power Management Unit (PMU) Requirements: The market research obtained from this request for information will be used to support a Government decision on the award of additional CCS Meadowlands systems between seven and up to an additional 24 systems. The intent for any future systems to follow the same design and functionality as the existing Meadowlands systems for efficiency in sustainment, training and and maintenance for the operational units. Additional Background Information Please contact the PCO should additional background information be required. Schedule and Key Deliverables: The Government may decide to hold an Industry Day at some point in the future. Should that Industry Day occur, contractors will be notified of the date and meeting details to allow for their attendance. SOC Administrative Requirements: The Government requests a maximum 10-page response in total with a 3-page limit for Company Information and Corporate Capabilities & Experience. Please submit via email to all the following points of contact: Contracting Officer: Lakisha Porter Contracting Officer Email: lakisha.porter@spaceforce.mil Program Manager: Captain Brandon Goulet Program Manager Email: brandon.goulet@spaceforce.mil Program Manager: Captain Eric Honeyman Program Manager Email: eric.honeyman@spaceforce.mil Response Content: Interested vendors must submit a Statement of Capability (SOC) in a narrative report that includes both the company/corporate information, solutions to the technical areas above and responses to the questions below. All SOCs are to be submitted in accordance with the administrative requirements identified herein. Submitted SOCs must include all of the following information: Company Information Corporate Capabilities & Experience Solutions and Identifying Risks for Key Technologies Answers to Technical Questions Answers to Contractual/Business Questions Company Information: 1. title: Germany – Purchase of CO2 emission credits – Dynamic Purchasing System for the Offsetting of the ECB's Greenhouse Gas Emissions
description: Since 2010, the ECB implements an environmental management system (EMS) in accordance with the international standard ISO 14001:2015 and Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2017/1505 and 2018/2026. The priority of the ECB remains to prevent greenhouse gas emissions wherever possible, limiting emissions in areas in which they cannot be avoided. Where emissions cannot be further limited and as greenhouse gas emissions cannot currently be reduced to zero, the ECB decided to offset its greenhouse gas emissions expressed in tonnes of CO2 equivalent as a complementary measure to its mitigation efforts (2021: 16 023,2 tonnes of CO2). The ECB envisages launching a dynamic purchasing system with a duration of initially two years, extendable at the ECB's option by another two years (total duration up to four years).

title: FCCD-ACM-MJ Support Services
description: Introduction/Background The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center (DEVCOM AC) Munitions Engineering Technology Center (METC), Medium and Cannon Caliber Munitions Division FCDD-ACM-MJ at Picatinny Arsenal, NJ is issuing this sources sought notice to conduct market research to determine the ability to perform complete life cycle engineering for a wide variety of munition systems across DEVCOM AC for various customers. This includes exploratory, advanced and engineering development, experimental testing, quality engineering, evaluation and qualification of munition systems and component concepts, as well as production and manufacturing engineering for munition systems and components. 2.Disclaimer THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A �REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)� TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. 3.Requirements: 3.1 The Contractor shall provide qualified engineering professionals to perform comprehensive engineering functions supporting the research, design, development, test and evaluation, production, and sustainment of advanced munition systems. The Contractor shall apply engineering competencies to solve complex technical challenges throughout the munition system lifecycle by executing rigorous engineering activities. The Contractor shall apply core engineering disciplines by executing critical technical activities such as performing requirements decomposition and system architecture design; creating detailed Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models; conducting structural, thermal, and kinematic finite element analysis (FEA); designing analog and digital circuit boards; developing embedded software and control algorithms; and formulating developmental test plans alongside post-test data reduction. Through these tasks, the Contractor shall deliver engineering artifacts such as Interface Control Documents (ICDs), Technical Data Packages (TDPs), simulation reports, and software version descriptions and actively participate in formal/informal reviews to ensure robust engineering rigor, standard methodologies, and scientific discipline are applied to the development, production, and sustainment of the munition systems. They will review designs and Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) against military and commercial specifications, Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) standards, and producibility standards and proactively identifying opportunities to reduce costs, accelerate schedules, optimize manufacturing processes, and elevate overall quality. Throughout the life cycle, the contractor shall be responsible for supporting project preparation encompassing planning, cost analysis, scheduling, facility coordination, and integration. Finally, they shall be responsible for collaborating with multi-disciplinary program teams to support the reliable delivery and sustained performance of munition systems, aligning all efforts with operational utility and organizational mission requirements. 3.2 The individuals are expected to travel on a semi-regular basis. 3.3 The Contractor shall attend, support, and report on meetings, review documents, contribute to the preparation of original documents, analyze cost, performance, risk, and provide recommendations or courses of action and ensure objectives are met. 3.4 The Contractor shall support the generation and review of briefing materials. 3.5 The Contractor shall support, coordinate, participate, and record regular Integrated Product Team (IPT) meetings on assigned projects/programs. 3.6 The Contractor shall provide technical advice regarding project feasibility, definitions of project scope, complexities/risk involved, phases required, and time schedules. 3.7 The Contractor shall keep project team leads/ Armaments Project Officer (APO) and Branch and Division supervisors informed of program/project status, issues, problems and recommendations through oral communication, proper documentation including trip reports and attendance at regularly scheduled and informal meetings. Provide technical support and advice to project team leads/APOs and Branch and Division supervisors on engineering aspects of assigned munition systems. This shall include solution recommendations regarding major problems and conflicting requirements with assigned projects/programs. 4. Background The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 541330 Engineering Services and the PSC code is R425 Engineering and Technical Services. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capability statement. 5. Submission Details Interested contractors are strongly encouraged to submit a capabilities statement with the following information: 5.1 Ability to provide a product that meets the above specifications. 5.2 Historical information demonstrating that you have the ability to provide the product (contract number(s), dollar value(s), Point of Contacts, and brief description of work performed). 5.3 In addition, please provide full company name and address, point of contact with telephone number and email address, CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, size of business (i.e. large, small, disadvantaged, veteran owned, woman owned, etc.) and applicable NAICS, Product Service Code (PSC), and website (if applicable). All data should be provided at no cost to the US Government by October 3, 2026 at 3PM EDT. 5.4 Contractors must be properly registered in the Government System for Award Management database (SAM). Contractors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation of requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220, or via the Internet at www.sam.gov. 5.5 This is a market survey for information only and shall not be construed as a request for a proposal or as an obligation on the part of the US Government. The US Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for information solicited. 5.6 The official response must be submitted to: The US Army Contracting Command - Rock Island at Picatinny, ATTN: Contracting/Agreements Officer: Charlotte Sylvain-Ceraul, charlotte.a.sylvain-ceraul.civ@army.mil and Contract Specialist: Qendresa Neza, qendresa.neza.civ@army.mil. Phone inquiries will not be addressed; all requests should be submitted in writing via email. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the survey.

Sole Source Justification JA-2026-03-8045 - TSA STIP SETA Bridge Support
description: This sole-source justification provides authority to award a task order on the basis of other than full and open competition for Systems Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA) support services. The contractor will perform SETA services to assist the SC Security Technology Integration Program (STIP) in system development and operations and maintenance (O&M). This includes providing technical guidance throughout the acquisition lifecycle and systems engineering life cycle (SELC), reviewing open architecture (OA), System of Systems (SoS), design documentation, and supporting risk management activities. The contractor will also assist in developing and maintaining documentation, reviewing operational processes for compliance and efficiency, supporting incident response and troubleshooting, and execution of major initiatives within STIP and related security technology efforts. These services will ensure accurate reporting and device connectivity to TSANetwork (TSANet) via the Security Technology Information eXchange (STIX) for alarm counts and throughput data. The contractor will validate the accuracy and integrity of system-generated reports, support improvements to reporting tools, and ensure compliance with Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and TSA data standards. Additionally, the contractor will review and validate device integration with TSANet, verify data transmission protocols, and assist in resolving connectivity issues to ensure reliable data collection and aggregation. STIP is the interface of Secure Flight (SF), Credential Authentication Technology CAT 2 (CAT-2), enhanced metal detectors (EMDs), and connectivity of other Transportation Security Equipment (TSE). These TSEs enhance the capabilities necessary to sustain TSA�s mission-critical operations, equip the frontline, and safeguard the traveling public. STIP provides the connection between TSEs located in airports and the TSANet for sharing of mission, and operational and maintenance data. Specifically, STIP enables network connectivity for exchanging the near-real time passenger vetting status of more than 1.7 million passengers daily between TSA�s SF system and over 2,100 CAT / CAT-2 units deployed at airports across the country. Without a STIP connection, that data cannot be shared with the checkpoints and data is performed manually by Transportation Security Officers (TSOs) on an hourly basis. SETA support services are paramount to providing technical monitoring of the STIP platform including analysis of vulnerabilities to the system and identification of process improvements and efficiencies to current and continuous operational changes. Only B&B can provide the required continuity of services with the highest level of confidence while maintaining support for active and time-sensitive SC initiatives and operations and maintenance services. These SC initiatives include ensuring successful management and completion of Advanced Imaging Technology (AIT) connectivity, Security Technology Information eXchange (STIX) connectivity, and operational utility evaluation (OUE) activities by November 2026; ensuring successful management and completion of the STIP database server migration to Windows Server 19 by January 2027; ensuring successful completion and operational readiness of the Data Center 15 (DC15) development lab by March 2027; and ensuring successful management and completion of ongoing STIP engineering change requests (ECRs), enhancements, and O&M. +++++++++++++
